hook.text: Remove every cell from blood and you're left with plasma: a yellowish liquid that makes up 55% of blood volume.

buildup.text: Plasma is 92% water. It carries hormones, nutrients, waste, antibodies, and clotting factors throughout the body.

discovery.text: Albumin, a plasma protein, maintains osmotic pressure. It keeps fluid inside blood vessels instead of leaking out.

twist.text: Liver failure reduces albumin. Without it, fluid leaks into tissues. That's why liver disease causes abdominal swelling.

climax.text: Donated plasma treats burn victims, hemophilia, and immune disorders. It's separated from whole blood and stored frozen.

punchline.text: The liquid half of blood carries everything cells can't.

quiz.question: What does albumin do in plasma?
options: Keeps fluid inside blood vessels via osmotic pressure
